title: H2 Structured Questions by Topic
doc: 2e H2 Structured Questions by Topic v0.12.docx

sections.title: 1. What this doc is and how it was built
bullets: All H2 structured questions (30 marks each): Paper 1 Q1 (Cluster 1), Paper 1 Q2 (Cluster 2) and Paper 2 Q2 (Cluster 3). That is 141 questions from 47 school-years, with 549 diagrams (438 pages, 61 MB).

Grouped by cluster, then by syllabus topic, then by school and year: 1.1 Environment and Resources (22), 1.2 Development and the Global Economy (25), 2.1 Tropical Climates and Drainage Basins (20), 2.2 Landforms in the Tropics (27), 3.1 Cities in a Sustainable Future (28), 3.2 The Future with Climate Change (19).
Under each question heading, a 'Syllabus' line lists every key question its parts test, most marks first (as in doc 1).
Question wording is typed from each school's question paper; diagrams are cropped from the school's Insert.
Checks run on every question: part labels in order, marks add up to 30, and labels and marks match the reading notes (all 141 match). Every diagram was checked by eye.

sections.title: 2. Assumptions
bullets: A question is filed under the topic with the most marks. 81 questions test two topics; for each one I counted marks part by part. In 62 the first-listed key question's topic has the most marks. In 6 the two topics tie, and the first-listed one is used. In 13 the other topic has more marks, so the question is filed there (section 3).
Two questions also test a key question from another cluster (CJC 2025 P1 Q2: 1.1.3b; HCI 2025 P1 Q1: 2.2.3c). They stay in their own paper's cluster.
Diagrams for a question are the resources its wording refers to, not the Insert's 'for Question N' labels.
Word files were converted to PDF with LibreOffice before extracting text and cropping, so line breaks and spacing can differ slightly from the printed paper.
Pages or pictures printed sideways are turned upright. Very tall diagrams are split across pages at blank lines instead of being shrunk to one page.
Diagrams are compressed (max 1300 px, JPEG or 256-colour PNG). Fine print in dense tables may be slightly softer than the original.
The section line is standardised: 'Section A — Cluster 1 / Cluster 2' for Paper 1 and 'Section B — Cluster 3' for Paper 2.

sections.title: 6. To consider
bullets: The file is large (61 MB). It could be split into three files, one per cluster, which would also suit revising one cluster at a time.
Group each topic further by key question. Many questions test four or five key questions, so this would mean listing a question more than once.
Add a contents list at the start (school and year, with page numbers), and start each question on a new page for printing.
